- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.5) after a recent dip, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior high), model often overcorrects downward — adjust downward bias by 3–7% to avoid premature reversal.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and price is falling, model underestimates support — add 2–5% to forecast to avoid bottoming too early.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the first 5–7 days of a new trend — apply a 3–6% upward bias for early horizon (1–7 days).
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by 1–3% downward for 3–5 day horizon.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast by 2–5% for 10–15 day horizon.
- Model tends to underestimate true price in 20–30 day horizon when sentiment is neutral — add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model overestimates upside — reduce forecast by 3–6% to avoid overconfidence in reversal.
